name: ModelRouter
purpose: Select a concrete model handle for a request based on declared policy (cheapest-first, quality-floor, tenant override) and fall back to the next candidate on rate limit, timeout, or provider error.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Sequence

class RoutePolicy(Protocol):
    candidates: tuple[str, ...]
    quality_floor: str
    budget_usd_cents: int

class ModelRouter(Protocol):
    def choose(self, policy: RoutePolicy, tenant_id: str) -> str: ...
    def failover(self, exhausted: Sequence[str], policy: RoutePolicy) -> str: ...
invariants: choose() MUST honour the policy's quality_floor; a candidate below the floor CANNOT be returned even when it is cheapest.
failover() MUST NEVER return a handle present in the exhausted list within the same request scope.
The router SHALL refuse to route when the tenant's BudgetGuard reports the tenant is over budget.
Routing decisions MUST be recorded with the chosen handle and reason so fallback chains are reconstructable.
Tenant overrides SHALL take precedence over global policy and CANNOT be silently ignored by default policy.
extension_contract: Projects add custom strategies (e.g., canary routing) by implementing a RoutePolicy provider and registering it; the router composes registered strategies via a middleware chain whose order is declared at boot.

sources.locator: Router class: model_list with weights, fallbacks, and rpm/tpm limits
Config: routing strategies (loadbalance, fallback, conditional) and retry semantics

why_essential: Provider outages and rate limits are routine; single-provider call sites either crash or silently degrade, while a shared router expresses failover policy declaratively.
alternatives_considered: Try/except around one provider SDK — no visibility into why it fell back, no policy.
Client-side round-robin — cannot honour quality floors or tenant overrides.
